meta.note: Preview data. All records are Awaiting Evidence Review. Descriptions were drawn from publisher and repository pages retrieved on this date and are not a substitute for the full papers.

items.q: What would count as evidence of subjective experience?

notes.text: Researchers disagree about what the theories require, and it is unclear whether current theories can be empirically distinguished.
A preregistered test of two theories reported results that partly align with each and substantially challenge key claims of each.

items.q: Can consciousness exist independently of biological neural systems?

notes.text: The 2023 AI consciousness report concludes that no current AI systems appear to be conscious and finds no obvious barriers to building conscious AI systems. The report is a preprint.
The 2004 IIT paper states that the theory implies consciousness could in principle be built into artificial systems.

items.q: Can similar behavior emerge from fundamentally different mechanisms?
What distinguishes information processing from conscious experience?

notes.text: Different theories locate the difference differently: in broadcast to many processors (GNWT), in irreducible cause-effect structure (IIT), in higher-order representation (HOT), or in a model of attention (AST).

items.q: What would a meaningful test of machine consciousness require?

notes.text: One report proposes assessing AI systems against indicator properties derived from several theories. Those indicators depend on theories that remain unsettled.

items.q: Can competing theories make experimentally distinguishable predictions?

notes.text: A preregistered protocol states contrasting predictions of GNWT and IIT, and a 2025 report describes the first results.
